result.summary: The pedestrian environment includes basic infrastructure such as sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, though the markings are significantly faded and worn. The wide roadway and lack of physical buffers or traffic calming measures suggest a car-oriented design that may prioritize vehicle speed over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are heavily worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the side street

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the sidewalk and the active travel lanes.

hazards.name: Wide corner radius
hazards.description: The intersection corner appears to have a wide radius, which can encourage higher vehicle speeds during right turns.
hazards.location_in_image: Left corner near the fire hydrant

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility ladder or zebra markings using durable thermoplastic material.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture
interventions.description: Add street trees or other vertical elements to create a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, continuous concrete sidewalk in front of a mixed-use building with a commercial ground floor. While the walkway is unobstructed, there is no physical buffer or street furniture separating pedestrians from the adjacent roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer, such as a planting strip or parked cars, between the wide sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: The curb line along the bottom edge of the sidewalk

hazards.name: Absence of street lighting
hazards.description: No street light poles are visible in the immediate vicinity, which may reduce safety and visibility at night.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with street trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and perceived safety for pedestrians using the walkway after dark.

result.summary: This is a two-way residential street with sidewalks on both sides but no marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. The roadway lacks lane markings, and the pedestrian environment is constrained by narrow effective widths due to utility poles and building stairs encroaching on the walkway.

hazards.name: Lack of lane markings
hazards.description: The absence of a center line or edge markings can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles on the right and building stairs on the left narrow the effective walking width for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the street without designated space or warning signs for drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to provide designated pedestrian space and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Paint center lines and parking lane markings to organize traffic flow and narrow the perceived travel lane, which can help reduce speeds.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a paved sidewalk adjacent to a mixed-use building, but lacks a buffer from the roadway. There is a notable absence of crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps at the visible corner, and a large blank wall section reduces natural surveillance.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian-Vehicle Separation
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the travel lane, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Poor Corner Sightlines
hazards.description: The building is situated at the property line, creating a blind corner for pedestrians and turning vehicles at the intersection.
